entries.title: No password or service_role key in the repo, ever
entries.what: config.js carries only the project URL, the publishable (anon) key and the staff email. Grep for secrets before every commit.
entries.why: The repo is public — GitHub Pages' free tier requires it. The publishable key is safe because RLS restricts the table to signed-in staff; the service_role key bypasses RLS entirely.

entries.title: Escape when drawing, not when storing
entries.what: Every user-typed value goes through escapeHtml at render time.
entries.why: Storing escaped text corrupts the data and breaks CSV exports. Escaping at the boundary where it becomes markup is the only place it is reliably correct.

entries.title: Trust nothing in the payments/refunds columns
entries.what: safeDataUrl() only lets through a data: URL of one of four types, base64 only. Anything else renders as an unreadable slot and refuses to open.
entries.why: Anyone with the staff password can write those jsonb columns straight over the REST API, never touching the form. An unescaped dataUrl was stored XSS on every other manager's phone.

entries.title: A new database column needs the probe pattern
entries.what: Add to schema.sql (create + alter-if-not-exists), add the name to COLUMN_OK, guard the write, grey the control out with a note, document the SQL in the README.
entries.why: The push is instant and the SQL is manual, so there is always a window where the site is ahead of the database. Without the guard, every save fails in that window — in a venue, at night.

entries.title: Nothing tappable under 40px
entries.what: Buttons, chips, tabs and close controls are at least 40px tall.
entries.why: This is used one-handed, standing up, mid-shift.

entries.title: Supabase and github.io are unreachable from the build session
entries.what: The egress proxy blocks supabase.com, *.supabase.co and github.io. The live site and real database cannot be opened from here.
entries.why: Everything is verified against a local fake Supabase instead. Say this plainly rather than implying the live site was checked.

entries.title: Only what is committed survives
entries.what: The session runs in a throwaway container. Anything outside the git repo — installed packages, ~/.claude config, scratch files — is gone when it ends.
entries.why: It is why this memory lives in the repo rather than in an agent's config directory.

entries.title: Alex runs a pub, not a codebase
entries.what: Explain the one manual step clearly and early. Screenshots beat descriptions. Own a bug directly when it is mine.
entries.why: The app is live in a working venue; a broken save is a real problem at 9pm on a Saturday.

entries.title: Lists are chronological, never urgency-sorted
entries.what: All tabs order by date. The old urgencyScore is gone.
entries.why: Sorting by urgency put a deposit chase two weeks out above an event tomorrow, and the board looked shuffled.

entries.title: Area chips widen the list, they don't narrow it
entries.what: Ticking Front Bar and Whole Venue shows both.
entries.why: Managers filter to 'the rooms I care about tonight', not to an intersection — an AND of two areas is always empty.

entries.title: Nothing is ever deleted on its own
entries.what: Events more than two days past prompt on open; a human clears or reschedules each one.
entries.why: Asked for explicitly. A booking that vanishes by itself is indistinguishable from one that was never saved.

entries.title: "Taken by" never pre-fills
entries.what: The field is blank on every new booking and must be typed.
entries.why: It used to remember the last name used on that phone. On a shared handset that quietly attributed bookings to whoever used it last.

entries.title: The booking sheet holds a fixed height
entries.what: #bookingDialog is 92dvh tall and scrolls internally; the header is sticky.
entries.why: Sizing to content made the bottom-anchored sheet shrink when fields hid, sliding its top edge and the ✕ down the screen mid-tap.

entries.title: Tabs wrap onto a second line
entries.what: The tab strip is flex-wrap, not overflow-x with a fade.
entries.why: The fourth tab, Past, sat off the right edge of a phone where nobody found it.

entries.title: Restaurant takes no deposit; anything else can waive one
entries.what: Restaurant is deposit-free by area. Every other area has a 'No deposit needed' tick. Deposit statuses drop out of the Status list when no deposit applies.
entries.why: A table booking is not a buyout, and large ticketed nights sometimes take the money on the door.

entries.title: The T&Cs render from one TERMS array
entries.what: Both the dialog and the 'Copy all' text build from TERMS at the top of the script.
entries.why: Alex updates the wording periodically; two copies would drift.

entries.title: A planted receipt could run code on every phone
entries.what: fileThumb and openLightbox interpolated f.dataUrl and f.id straight into HTML, and framed anything whose type field claimed application/pdf.
entries.why: Fixed by validating the data URL and escaping the attributes. Verified with an actual attack row written straight to the database.

entries.title: Picking an area moved the ✕ out from under the thumb
entries.what: The sheet was bottom-anchored and content-sized, so hiding the deposit block slid its top edge down — measured at 111px, and 387px once a scroll position clamped.
entries.why: Reported as 'it messes up and presses everything'. Invisible in a test until the ✕ position was measured before and after.

entries.title: Someone else's name kept appearing on new bookings
entries.what: A remembered name in localStorage pre-filled 'Taken by' on a shared phone.
entries.why: Reported as 'it keeps saying Damon'. A convenience feature quietly corrupting an accountability field.

entries.title: The Past tab was invisible on a phone
entries.what: The tab strip scrolled sideways with a fade that read as decoration rather than as 'there is more'.

entries.title: The board looked shuffled
entries.what: An urgency score outranked the date, so a deposit chase weeks away sat above tomorrow night's event.

entries.title: A more specific selector silently un-hid a hidden field
entries.what: .auth-card input (0,1,1) beat .visually-hidden (0,1,0), so the hidden username field was a full screen wide and pushed the sign-in screen sideways.
entries.why: Utility classes lose to component selectors. Name the element in the utility rule too.

entries.title: The browser's own popup hid the styled errors
entries.what: required fired the native bubble before the custom inline messages could show. The form carries novalidate; the attributes stay for semantics.
entries.why: Only showed up on a real click, never in code that called the submit handler directly.

entries.title: accept="" on a file input is not validation
entries.what: A PDF is verified by its first bytes (%PDF-); images must genuinely decode and are re-encoded to JPEG.
entries.why: The picker's filter is trivially bypassed — an HTML file named receipt.pdf sailed through.

entries.title: frame-ancestors does nothing in a meta CSP
entries.what: It only works as a real HTTP header, and GitHub Pages cannot send headers. connect-src is the directive that earns its place here.
entries.why: Worth stating rather than implying the page is protected against framing.

entries.title: The CSP blocks the local fake database
entries.what: The scratch copy needs 127.0.0.1 added to connect-src. Test the shipped policy separately against the untouched file.
entries.why: Otherwise you are either testing a policy nobody ships, or not testing the app at all.

entries.title: No charset meant broken apostrophes
entries.what: The standalone build had no <meta charset="utf-8">, so curly quotes and emoji rendered as mojibake.

entries.title: A failed edit in a batch discards the whole batch
entries.what: One patch script exited on a bad match after earlier replacements had been applied in memory, so the file was never written and two changes vanished silently.
entries.why: Only the test caught it. Verify what actually landed rather than trusting the script printed something.

entries.title: A memory file does not make a session start knowing things
entries.what: Every session begins blank. This store still has to be read; structure changes how much is read, not whether reading happens.
entries.why: Asked for a graph so re-reading would not be needed. Worth saying plainly rather than implying the tool learns.

entries.title: Spawning agents usually costs more tokens, not fewer
entries.what: Every subagent starts cold and re-derives context the orchestrator already has. Three agents on a small change can cost several times doing it directly.
entries.why: The build-crew skill exists to route work to the cheapest capable model and to spawn only what is needed — not to always use five. The routing gate at the top of that skill is the part that saves anything.

entries.title: An explicit display beats the hidden attribute
entries.what: Toggling el.hidden does nothing when the element has its own display rule. .fab, .stats and .tabs each needed an explicit [hidden]{display:none}.
entries.why: Bit twice — first on the deposit block, then on the New booking / New event swap, where both buttons showed at once.

entries.title: Events live on their own board and their own table
entries.what: A top-left switch swaps the whole page between bookings and events. Events are a separate table with no pax, deposit or organiser.
entries.why: A booking is something the venue sold; an event is something happening in Sydney that fills the place regardless. Forcing them into one table would have meant half the fields being meaningless on every row.

entries.title: What an event records, and what it drops
entries.what: Title, kind, sport, round, date, time, streaming channel, expected crowd, on-the-screens with which screens, sound on, notes. Sport and round only appear on a Sport; which-screens only when it is going on. Anything hidden is cleared on save.
entries.why: In a pub the operational questions are which screens and whether the commentary goes through the PA instead of the music — those cause arguments on the night. The channel matters because free-to-air and a subscription we do not have are very different problems.

entries.title: Events clear themselves two hours after they start
entries.what: pruneFinishedEvents() runs after every load and deletes events more than EVENT_KEEP_HOURS past their start. One with no time survives to the end of its day. An unparseable date is left alone.
entries.why: An explicit exception to never-auto-delete, and the reason the two differ: a booking is a commercial record, an event is a heads-up that is pure clutter once the game has been and gone.

entries.title: A week of fixtures arrives as one paste, not as SQL
entries.what: The Paste button takes pipe-separated lines, previews what it found, flags unreadable lines and skips duplicates by date+title.
entries.why: Supabase is unreachable from the build session, so research could only be handed over as SQL to paste into the dashboard. That is a poor weekly chore. This keeps it inside the app on a phone, and goes through the normal save path so RLS still applies.

entries.title: A flex item will not shrink below its own content
entries.what: Adding a button beside the search input overflowed at 320px until the input got min-width:0.
entries.why: min-width:auto is the default on a flex item. Caught only by the width audit, not by looking at it.
